sources.excerpt: Docmost is available in two editions for self-hosted deployments: Open Source and Enterprise. Open Source is free to use and includes all core documentation and collaboration features. It is available under the AGPL-3.0 license. Enterprise includes everything in the open source edition, plus additional features designed for larger teams and organizations. You need an enterprise license key to unlock enterprise features.

sources.excerpt_normalization: Unicode source text with all whitespace runs collapsed to one ASCII space and outer whitespace removed.
sources.excerpt: Enterprise Edition Features: Bases (Table and Kanban views); SSO (SAML 2.0 / OIDC); LDAP; SCIM provisioning; MFA (TOTP); AI (AI Chat, AI-powered writing assistance, AI-powered search, and MCP); API (REST API with personal API keys and admin key management); full-text search in attachments; resolve comments; disable public sharing; Confluence importer; DOCX importer; PDF importer; Templates; page-level permissions; and page verification and approval workflow. Import / Export includes Markdown and HTML formats and ZIP archive import.

sources.excerpt: To automatically provision users upon their first login, enable the Allow Signup toggle. To activate this integration immediately, enable the Enabled toggle. After successful configuration, the OIDC provider appears as an available login method. Docmost reads groups from the groups or roles claim in the userinfo response. The claim can be an array of strings or a single comma- or semicolon-separated string. Groups must be pre-created in Docmost; OIDC group synchronization does not create new groups. Matching is case-insensitive. Configure the OIDC provider to include a groups or roles claim in the userinfo response or ID token.
used_for: OIDC provider UI, signup, enabled login, and group synchronization

sources.excerpt: To automatically provision users on first login, enable the Allow Signup option. Activate this integration immediately by toggling Enabled. Once successfully configured, the SAML provider appears on the login page. Docmost reads groups from groups, Groups, memberOf, memberof, roles, Roles, http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/Group, http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/groups, http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/role, and http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/role. Group values can be a multi-value attribute or a single comma- or semicolon-separated string. Groups must be pre-created in Docmost and matching is case-insensitive.
used_for: SAML provider UI, signup, enabled login, aliases, and group synchronization

sources.excerpt: LDAP group sync enables automatic synchronization of LDAP groups to Docmost groups. Allow Signup allows new users to be automatically provisioned on first login. The user authentication flow binds with the configured service account, searches for the user, validates user credentials by binding as the user, retrieves user attributes (email, name, groups), creates or updates the user account, and synchronizes group memberships if enabled. Groups must be pre-created in Docmost with names that match LDAP group names. When enabling LDAP for existing users, users with matching email addresses are linked to LDAP accounts, LDAP login updates their profile with LDAP attributes, and syncs groups if enabled.
used_for: LDAP verified identity, safe linking, profile update, signup, and group mapping

sources.excerpt: While SCIM is enabled, it takes precedence over SSO group sync. Group memberships are controlled by the identity provider. Supported user operations are list, get, create, replace, update, and deactivate user. DELETE /Users/:id deactivates the user in Docmost; it does not erase their data. Supported group operations are list, get, create, replace, update, and delete. The default Everyone group cannot be updated or deleted via SCIM. Only the eq filter operator is supported. User filters are userName, email, id, externalId, and active. Group filters are displayName, id, and externalId. Pagination startIndex defaults to 1 and count defaults to and is limited to 100. Groups created via SCIM are marked as external and their members are managed by the identity provider. When SCIM is enabled, it is the source of truth for group memberships and SSO-based group synchronization is ignored.
used_for: SCIM filters, deactivation, Everyone protection, and group-source precedence

sources.excerpt: The profile scope includes basic profile information, such as the user's username, name, and group membership. In authentik releases before 2025.10, the email scope always set the email_verified claim to True. Starting with authentik 2025.10, email_verified defaults to False. Some applications require this claim to be True before allowing users to authenticate. For greater security, verify users' email addresses and store the verification status as a user attribute, then configure the scope mapping to return that value dynamically.

sources.excerpt: If the service provider supports patch updates, authentik uses patch requests to add or remove members of groups. For other user and group updates, authentik uses PUT requests. With default settings, the unique user IDs in SCIM and other protocols are identical, allowing applications to link provisioned users with users signing in through OAuth/OIDC or SAML. Applications can match users on externalId, email, or username.
